simple.meaning: שְׁבַשׁ (shᵉbash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to entangle , i.e. perplex.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 5:9. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁבַשׁ (H7672) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שְׁבַשׁ (shᵉbash) / H7672 is traced through Daniel 5:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7672. shebash [ שְׁבַשׁ ] verb Hithpa`el be perplexed ( ᵑ7 id., entangle, beguile , Late Hebrew שָׁבַשׁ confuse, disarrange ; compare Assyrian šabâšu (šabasu), turn about; Syriac flatter, allure , Schulth Hom. Wurz. 90 ; so Mandean Pa`el שבש Nö M 49 ; compare Arabic (as loan-word Nö l.c .) confuse ); — Participle plural מִשְׁתַּבְּשִׁין Dan 5:9 .

occurrences.englishText: Then king Belshazzar was greatly troubled, and his face was changed in him, and his lords were perplexed.
